title: Unified on-prem K8s deploy strategy (vSphere + Baremetal, ephemeral nodes) — WIP
content:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a single, opinionated playbook for provisioning and upgrading on-prem Kubernetes clusters that need to support both vSphere and bare‑metal (IPMI/iPXE) environments. Goal: minimize divergent operational paths by standardizing bootstrapping primitives, Terraform module interfaces, and an upgrade choreography that works across both platforms.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target clusters: control-plane HA (3 nodes), worker pools ephemeral by default (stateless BS/compute) with a separate stateful pool for storage workloads.
- Kubernetes distribution: kubeadm-managed upstream clusters (we evaluate RKE2/k0s later but keep kubeadm for control).
- Storage: vSphere CSI for vSphere, Ceph/Rook or Longhorn for baremetal stateful workloads.
- Networking: Calico (BGP) preferred for baremetal; vSphere installs can use Calico with VDS or Antrea when constrained.
- PXE/provisioning: iPXE + cloud-init for baremetal; vSphere Content Library/OVA templates + cloud-init for VM provisioning.
- TF modules: keep module inputs consistent across providers so product teams can use same higher-level module.

High level flow (single command intent):
1) terraform apply bootstrap-networking (VLANs, DNS entries, IPAM reservations)
2) terraform apply infra (vSphere VMs or metal provision jobs)
3) bootstrap control-plane via kubeadm remote-exec or ssh (with systemd units & kubeadm-config stored in secrets)
4) join workers with ignition/cloud-init pointing to token endpoint
5) install CSI, CNI, metrics, ingress, and monitoring
6) run acceptance tests and promote cluster to "ready"

Terraform module notes / conventions (opinionated):
- Top-level module names: redwood.vsphere, redwood.baremetal, redwood.k8s-cluster
- Each module exposes the same k8s_cluster.* outputs (kubeconfig, control_plane_ips, cluster_id).
- Use provider aliasing: provider "vsphere" { } and provider "metal" { } for baremetal.
- Keep bootstrap tokens ephemeral and passed to cloud-init via a temp objectstore (minio) or short-lived Vault secret.
- Example minimal module interface (pseudocode):
  module "k8s_cluster" {
    source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//k8s-cluster"
    provider = var.provider_type // "vsphere" | "baremetal"
    control_plane_count = 3
    worker_pool = var.worker_pools
    k8s_version = var.k8s_version
    network = var.network_config
  }

Bootstrap specifics — vSphere:
- Prepare template image with cloud-init guestinfo support (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS base image, cloud-init 24.x).
- Use Content Library and VM cloning via vsphere_guest or ovf_deploy. Keep folder naming: /Clusters/{env}/{cluster_name}/controlplane.
- Pre-generate static IP allocations in IPAM and create DNS A records (terraform-managed).
- vsphere-cpi + vsphere-csi must be installed post-k8s control-plane readiness. CSI needs correct vCenter credentials (k8s secret) scoped to the cluster.

Bootstrap specifics — Baremetal (IPMI / iPXE):
- Workflow: IPMI power-cycle -> iPXE chainload -> initramfs cloud-init pulls user-data that runs kubeadm join or kubeadm init for control-plane; ephemeral worker nodes run a join script.
- Prefer image builder that outputs a rootfs + kernel + initrd set and two-stage iPXE kernel args to reduce provisioning time.
- Keep a small metal-provision service (simple Go binary) behind Terraform to record PXE boot tokens and correlate node meta -> k8s node name.

Cluster bootstrap idempotency:
- All bootstrap scripts must be safe to re-run: detect kubeadm init/join state, re-apply kubeadm config with --upload-certs as needed.
- Terraform should not manage post-join objects (helm installs, CRDs) to avoid drift: use Flux/Terragrunt or a separate GitOps flow.

Network considerations (practical notes):
- MTU: if environment has jumbo frames, ensure both infra and CNI are configured. Calico IP-in-IP or VXLAN options matter.
- BGP design: for baremetal we prefer Calico BGP with external route reflectors or metalLB in BGP mode for Service IPs.
- vSphere: if using NSX/VDS providing L2, prefer Antrea or Calico in overlay-free mode to reduce complexity.

Storage & HA notes:
- Stateful pools: zone-aware storage class mapping to PV topology. On baremetal prefer Ceph/Rook with CRUSH map reflecting racks/PDUs.
- vSphere: configure storage policy and vSAN (if present) and annotate StorageClass with reclaimPolicy and volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer.

Upgrade plan (applies across both providers):
- Goals: zero- or low-downtime control plane upgrade, safe worker upgrade with canaries, verified rollback path.
- Preflight checks (automated): API reachability, etcd health (member list), available control-plane capacity, PodDisruptionBudget headroom, CSI driver compatibility matrix.
- Canary control-plane upgrade: upgrade one control-plane node at a time with etcd snapshot before operation, validate etcd cluster after rejoin. Use kubeadm upgrade apply --allow-experimental-upgrades if needed.
- Worker upgrade flow: cordon -> drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -> kubeadm upgrade node -> ssh/agent run post-checks -> uncordon.
- Blue/green vs rolling: default to rolling with small batches. For high-risk changes (e.g., CRI runtime swap) use a blue-green with label-based service flip.
- Rollback: keep etcd snapshots in long-lived S3 (minio) daily and before upgrades; have documented restore step: restore etcd to snapshot on isolated control-plane, validate cluster API, then scale up workers.

Validation & smoke tests (post-upgrade):
- kube-system core pods healthy
- control-plane latency SLI: apiserver request latency < X ms (baseline), scheduler pressure tests
- run a synthetic end-to-end workload: deploy a simple job that performs 10x model inferences against local service (this validates CPU/memory constraints under real RPM)
- confirm CSI operations: provisioning a PVC, IO test, deletion

Observability hooks during deployment:
- Annotate each terraform apply with run_id and post logs to the cluster-ops channel.
- Enable temporary verbose metrics (kube-apiserver audit, kubelet verbose).
- Export perf traces to a central observability instance (tempo/jaeger) for latency spikes during control-plane changes.

Operational pitfalls (learned from prior runs):
- Token expiration forces rebootstrap; instead prefer ephemeral Vault token + small bootstrap service to mint node join tokens on-demand.
- vSphere tools: ensure guest tools do not auto-update the kernel before kubeadm-managed operations; we lock image to cloud-init only.
- Time sync: NTP/chrony misconfig causes certificate rotation headaches. Enforce chrony config in cloud-init.

Quick Terraform snippets (notes, not full modules):
- vsphere VM clone excerpt (pseudo):
  resource "vsphere_virtual_machine" "cp" {
    name = "${var.cluster_name}-cp-${count.index}"
    clone {
      template_uuid = data.vsphere_virtual_machine.template.id
    }
    lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["guest_id"] }
  }

- baremetal ipmi job (pseudo):
  resource "metal_provision_job" "node" {
    host_id = local.host_map[count.index]
    image = var.image_name
    user_data = file("./cloud-init/cp-cloudinit.yaml")
  }

Checklist for a safe control-plane upgrade (play-by-play):
- [ ] Create INF upgrade run ticket and link to run_id
- [ ] Backup etcd snapshot and store off-cluster (minio/S3)
- [ ] Verify all control-plane nodes Ready and etcd leader election stable
- [ ] Set cluster autoscaler to maintain min nodes (if autoscaler present)
- [ ] Upgrade kubeadm on the node to target version
- [ ] Run kubeadm upgrade apply on one control-plane node
- [ ] Validate etcd member health and API responsiveness for 10 minutes
- [ ] Proceed to next control-plane node
- [ ] Upgrade workers in batches (size configurable)
- [ ] Run post-upgrade smoke tests and sign-off

Open questions / TODOs (needs owners):
- Replace kubeadm bootstrap with a short-lived control-plane-as-a-service for initial bootstrap? (owner: Liam)
- Standardize image build pipeline (Packer vs custom build) and publish immutable version manifest (owner: Sofia)
- Add automated preflight CI job that runs the full upgrade checklist in a small-scale lab cluster (owner: Ethan)

Notes to self / gotchas: 
- Keep terraform state compartmentalized per environment. Avoid monolithic state for >50 nodes.
- Document exact cloud-init user-data versions; small whitespace or YAML parsing errors are frequent causes of bootstrap flakiness.
- When testing network MTU changes, test with actual model payloads (tokenized inputs) to catch unexpected fragmentation.

References and helpful links:
- Confluence: On-Prem K8s Patterns (see linked_artifacts)
- GitHub: terraform-modules repo (linked_artifacts)
- Jira: INF-1423 (upgrade automation epic)

End notes: This is intentionally a working sketch. The goal is to converge on a small, repeatable set of Terraform patterns and a single upgrade choreography that teams can rely on. Next steps: break this doc into three focused PRDs (bootstrap infra, terraform module interface, upgrade automation) and schedule a review with SRE and Applied ML for platform-specific test cases.
